subject.title: fix(github-copilot): prevent stale reasoning from breaking later turns

question: Should GitHub Copilot preserve provenance-approved encrypted reasoning within the active user turn, or unconditionally strip encrypted reasoning before every provider request?
rationale: The draft and the open maintainer-authored alternative choose different reliability-versus-reasoning-continuity policies, while the available mocked tests cannot establish Copilot’s actual token and connection lifetime contract.

options.title: Prove lineage-aware replay
options.body: Retain this draft’s active-turn policy if live sequential, parallel, and token-rotation runs confirm accepted replay and bounded recovery.

options.title: Strip all ciphertext
options.body: Adopt the smaller provider-boundary approach from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95493, sacrificing encrypted reasoning continuity to minimize provider-session failures.

options.title: Separate the fixes
options.body: Land drain-level recovery independently and defer the permanent Copilot replay policy until provider behavior is proven.

recommendation.title: Prove lineage-aware replay
recommendation.body: Retain this draft’s active-turn policy if live sequential, parallel, and token-rotation runs confirm accepted replay and bounded recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior GitHub Copilot work and member-authored competing PR make them the strongest available owner for the replay-policy choice.
